scoring_justification: The main result is a set of resistivity and TCR values from a complex self-consistent solver; recomputing them in the checker sandbox is infeasible due to heavy numerical integration and iterative solver. Therefore, T0 result-level compare against paper-reported values is used with 10% relative tolerance for resistivity and 20% for TCR.

hidden_assets.purpose: hidden gold resistivity and TCR values for Ag, Au, Fe, Ni, Eu from paper Table 2
hidden_assets.source_provenance: paper Table 2: calculated resistivity and TCR
hidden_assets.generation_method: extracted directly from paper Table 2: Ag: resistivity 23.161, TCR 29; Au: resistivity 79.46, TCR 6.6; Fe: resistivity 200.02, TCR 5.2; Ni: resistivity 94.328, TCR 3; Eu: resistivity 282.5, TCR -32.1. All resistivities in μΩ·cm, TCR in 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: values are the paper's own calculated results, verified against the paper's Table 2.

outputs.description: CSV with columns: metal (string, one of Ag/Au/Fe/Ni/Eu), resistivity (float), TCR (float). The checker compares each row to hidden gold values from the paper's reported Table 2 with tolerances.

output_contract.notes: The task uses the final adjusted parameters |V| and q0 directly from the paper (Table 2) without requiring the agent to perform the parameter fitting stage. The solver must implement the full KKR potential model, Percus-Yevick S(q), and the mode-coupling equations as described.
